description:
## Outcome

Each automation matrix cell creates one fresh Jidoka session and calls the public ordered sequence API once. The CLI no longer carries Jidoka agent state or computes cumulative operation offsets.

## Why now

This removes the main product-boundary violation. Later execution environments and extension hooks need one Jidoka-owned cell lifecycle.

## Current state

`lib/jido_cli/cli/automation/engine/jidoka.ex` starts a session, uses `Enum.reduce_while`, stores `agent_state`, injects it into the next `Turn.Request`, stores `operation_count`, and slices operation results. Existing tests prove continuity and turn-scoped assertions. Loader, Plan, matrix concurrency, JSONL, and artifacts are already complete and must remain unchanged.

## Ownership and boundary

This is a `jido_cli` change that consumes the public contract from the blocking Jidoka story. CLI still owns request metadata, scenario assertion evaluation, timing, result projection, JSONL, and exit status. Jidoka owns ordered execution, session state, operation deltas, and terminal sequence state.

## Detailed implementation

1. Build normal public request inputs for all scenario turns without `agent_state`.
2. Start the deterministic cell session and call `Jidoka.Session.run_sequence/3`.
3. Map each returned step to the existing turn record. Use Jidoka-provided operation deltas for `operation_called` assertions.
4. Preserve injected `id_generator`, clocks, runtime capabilities, cell/session ID, input, context, and automation metadata.
5. Map complete, error, hibernated, and cancelled sequence states to the existing execution and evaluation meanings.
6. Delete the manual reducer, continuation state, operation counter, and direct cumulative state slicing.
7. Keep `jido.case-result` version 1 unchanged in this story.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No CLI code adds `agent_state` to a later request.
- [ ] No CLI code tracks an operation result offset.
- [ ] A successful multi-turn scenario keeps state inside its one session.
- [ ] A tool call from turn 1 cannot pass a turn 2 assertion.
- [ ] Error or hibernation at turn N records the prefix and does not run N+1.
- [ ] A new matrix cell starts a distinct session.
- [ ] Current JSONL fields, stdout, stderr, and statuses 0, 1, and 64 stay stable.

## Test plan

- Success: update `test/jido_cli/cli/automation/engine/jidoka_test.exs` for memory and operation-scoping cases.
- Invalid input: keep invalid request data coverage and assert a turn-specific error.
- Runtime failure: fake LLM error, operation error, and hibernation at a selected turn.
- Boundary and security: source test proves no manual continuation state or Jidoka execution module call.
- Deterministic capability: inject fake LLM, operations, clocks, and IDs.
- JSONL and exit status: run automation, JSONL, CLI, and result tests for exact physical lines and 0/1/64 behavior.

## Documentation

Update the README implementation note only if the public sequence changes user-visible wording. Keep the documented one-fresh-session-per-cell rule.

## Non-goals

Do not change scenario version 1. Do not add assertions. Do not reorder concurrent cells. Do not add compare or validate commands. Do not add a second session per turn.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.2.1` — Add a public ordered Jidoka session sequence
- `jido_cli-tqg.1.1` — Use the sibling Jidoka checkout as the CLI development contract

Features unlocked by this story:

- Validated automation schemas
- Headless cancellation
- Execution-environment attachment to one cell

## Commit plan

Create exactly one focused `jido_cli` commit. Use a message such as `feat(cli): use Jidoka session sequences (jido_cli-tqg.2.2)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

## Verification commands

```sh
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jido_cli
mix test test/jido_cli/cli/automation/engine/jidoka_test.exs test/jido_cli/cli/automation_test.exs test/jido_cli/cli/automation/jsonl_test.exs
mix quality
mix test --cover
```
title: Run automation cells through the public Jidoka sequence
